profiles.meeting_scenario: A design review meeting at an industry speech ML lab evaluating whether to approve an internal replication-and-adaptation plan based on the paper 'Attention-based End-to-End Models for Small-Footprint Keyword Spotting.' The team wants to reuse the paper's attention-based CRNN keyword spotter as a candidate wake-word detector for a battery-constrained wearable device. The context is that the modeling proposal already exists, and this meeting is to judge whether the proposed design is sufficiently aligned with the lab's internal review bar before engineering time is committed. The agenda is to review the proposed architecture fit, check whether the evaluation plan is comparable to prior internal wake-word reviews, and decide what evidence is needed for approval. The expected outcome is a conditional go-ahead: agreement on a short list of artifacts Maya will provide for the next gate, with both participants believing they share the same interpretation of those artifacts.

members.name: Dr. Maya Chen
members.expertise: Neural acoustic modeling, attention mechanisms, low-parameter speech models, experimental design
members.background: Maya joined from a PhD and postdoc track in end-to-end speech recognition and now leads fast-turnaround model evaluations for on-device keyword spotting research.
members.private_state: She wants quick approval to run a clean paper-faithful replication before spending time on deployment-specific modifications, because she believes the scientific comparison will be more convincing if the model is kept as close to the publication as possible.
hidden_assumptions: A model counts as 'small-footprint' primarily by trainable parameter count, so an ~84K-parameter CRNN attention model clearly satisfies the footprint requirement even before runtime profiling.
Keeping 'the same frontend' means preserving the published 40-channel log-Mel feature configuration and training-side normalization recipe used in the research scripts.
Evaluating 'at 1 false alarm per hour' means selecting a threshold per model from a development set and then reporting FRR at that operating point on the held-out benchmark.
When discussing 'end-to-end latency,' the relevant boundary is the acoustic model's detection timing relative to the keyword frames, not downstream debounce or product confirmation logic.

members.name: Alex Romero
members.role: Applied ML Engineer, Edge Speech Systems
members.expertise: Streaming inference, embedded deployment, wake-word evaluation harnesses, on-device performance optimization
members.background: Alex has spent several product cycles integrating wake-word models into shipping wearable and smart-speaker stacks, and he typically reviews research proposals for compatibility with existing streaming infrastructure.
members.private_state: He wants any approved design to fit into the current deployment stack with minimal systems churn, because his team is already committed to a firmware schedule and cannot absorb a custom evaluation or frontend pipeline.
hidden_assumptions: A model is only truly 'small-footprint' if total on-device cost fits the target budget, including recurrent state, attention buffers, scratch RAM, and runtime compute on the wearable DSP path.
Keeping 'the same frontend' means reusing the production streaming feature extractor and normalization path already in the wake-word stack, including its online loudness handling.

Evaluating 'at 1 false alarm per hour' means using the standard continuous-stream replay harness and the team's usual detector conventions, including cooldown behavior and fixed thresholding practice from prior reviews.
When discussing 'end-to-end latency,' the relevant boundary includes buffering and post-score confirmation logic because that is what users experience in the shipped system.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say the proposed attention-based model should remain 'small-footprint.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Maya means the neural model should stay near the paper's parameter budget, roughly under 100K trainable parameters, regardless of temporary runtime overheads during a research prototype.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Alex means the full deployed detector path must fit the device's memory and compute envelope, including model state, attention context buffers, and per-chunk execution cost.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In speech ML discussions, 'small-footprint' is a standard positive label and both interpretations are common; because the paper itself foregrounds parameter count, and Alex is thinking about deployment by default, each hears the phrase as obviously sufficient without asking for a formal definition.

misalignment_points.topic: What it means to keep the same frontend
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree to 'keep the frontend the same' so the review focuses on the model change.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Maya means she will preserve the published feature recipe in the research pipeline: 40-dim log-Mel frames with the existing training-side normalization behavior used in her replication scripts.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Alex means the model should consume the current production streaming frontend outputs from the on-device stack, with its online normalization and feature computation conventions unchanged.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Using the 'same frontend' sounds like a straightforward control variable, so neither expects ambiguity; they are both imagining a stable feature extractor, but one is anchored to the paper-faithful research pipeline and the other to the shipping stack.

misalignment_points.topic: How to evaluate at 1 false alarm per hour
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree the replication should be judged 'at 1 FA/hour,' matching the paper-style headline number.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Maya means each candidate model can be tuned to its own threshold on a development split, and FRR will then be reported at that operating point on the held-out benchmark set.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Alex means the detector should satisfy the team's standard 1-FA/hour bar in the continuous replay harness under the usual detector settings, with thresholding interpreted the way prior internal wake-word reviews have done it.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The numeric operating point makes the discussion feel precise, so both assume the evaluation convention is already implied; because neither is debating the metric itself, the hidden difference in measurement protocol slips by.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both discuss whether 'end-to-end latency' will be acceptable for the design review.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Maya includes only the model-side detection timing implied by causal framing, encoder lookback, and the attention decision point relative to the spoken keyword.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Alex includes all latency the product stack introduces after scoring, such as chunk buffering, smoothing, and confirmation logic before the wake event is emitted.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are sincerely talking about user-visible responsiveness, but in research reviews model latency is often shorthand for acoustic detection timing while in deployment reviews it naturally expands to the whole trigger path; the phrase feels shared enough that neither thinks to redraw the boundary.
